conflicts.fact: Wording of the Embu farmer's testimony (the Lesson 7 teacher says it is read verbatim from Lesson 1)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 quote: 'My grandfather knew exactly when to plant maize. I no longer do.' (James Muriithi), with rains 3–4 weeks later. Lesson 7 reads 'verbatim' a different text: 'The long rains used to come in March, like clockwork. My grandmother planted by the sound of the first thunder...' with no named farmer and a wait until April or May.
Lesson 1: area shrank from ~1.35 km² in 1934 to under 0.20 km² in 2023 (about 85% loss of area). Lesson 5: Lewis Glacier lost over 90% of its mass since 1900, a different baseline year and metric.

conflicts.fact: Evidence Timeline in Lesson 7 misassigns the content and evidence of earlier lessons
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says: L1 PhET simulation; L2 charcoal/Mau data; L3 ozone/CFC data; L4 NASA temperature data and glacier measurements; L5 Olkaria/Turkana wind mitigation; L6 Turkana pastoralist and Mombasa testimonies. Actual: L1 glacier images and farmer testimony; L3 PhET; L4 NASA data and Lake Victoria; L5 Keeling Curve and human amplification; L6 ozone and CFCs. Mitigation and community testimonies appear in no earlier lesson.

conflicts.fact: Content of the Lesson 1 cumulative model, as described by later lessons
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: students draw an energy-balance model (sun energy, surface, atmosphere, link to glacier and rains). Lesson 3 says that in Lesson 1 they drew the physical layers of the atmosphere. Lesson 5 says that by Lesson 4 the model includes the ozone layer filtering UV, but ozone is not introduced until Lesson 6, which adds it as new.

conflicts.fact: When the ozone layer was taught
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 predict prompt says that Lessons 1–4 covered the ozone layer and the model includes an ozone layer. Lesson 6 introduces the ozone layer as new and adds it to the model for the first time.

conflicts.fact: Which Lesson 2 student task matches the model and the greenhouse gases
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 greenhouse gases include CO2, water vapour, CH4 and N2O. Lesson 2 model requires CO2, CH4 and N2O sources, while Lesson 3 describes mechanisms for CO2, H2O and CH4 only. This is a minor inconsistency in gas lists.

conflicts.fact: Moisture source for the long rains
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says warming increases evaporation from Lake Victoria and the Indian Ocean. Lesson 4 attributes it to the Indian Ocean and ITCZ shifts, and treats Lake Victoria as a flooding case.
Lesson 6 reframes the phenomenon as 'Why are UV levels in Nairobi rising' while the UV-B data it uses shows a peak in the late 1990s followed by decline, which contradicts 'rising' now.
